bin/todo inserts the repo root onto sys.path so `from todo import commands, store` resolves regardless of invocation cwd — not specified by the AC text but required for the entry point to be runnable from any directory.
deviations: T0 e2e_verification_fixtures #2-7 in scope-cli-core.md all fail (fixtures_passed 1/7 across 3 attempts, unchanged) due to a fixture-authoring bug, not an implementation defect: each fixture's inner `python3 -c "...\"$T/s.json\"..."` / `TODO_STORE=\"$T/s.json\"` construct uses backslash-escaped quotes inside a single-quoted `bash -c '...'` string. Single quotes in bash do not process backslash escapes, so the inner bash script receives literal `\"` sequences; its own parser then treats those as an escaped-literal-quote-character (not a quote delimiter), embedding literal `"` characters into values like TODO_STORE and turning `add \"ship it\"` into two arguments (`"ship`, `it"`) instead of one quoted argument. Reproduced directly: piping the exact fixture #2 string (as stored, JSON-decoded once) through `sh -c "<fixture>"` yields `todo: error: unrecognized arguments: it"` — an argparse error from the malformed quoting, not from bin/todo's logic. I confirmed the intended behavior manually by running the same assertions with normal (unescaped) quoting substituted for the fixture's inner shell logic against this implementation, and it passed (ADD_OK / LIST_OK / DONE_OK / RM_OK / CORRUPTED_UNIFORM_OK / INV05_DEFAULT_PATH_OK equivalents all printed, matching every use case's Test Surface row and error-message wording verbatim). I did not modify scope-cli-core.md — it is outside this order's substrate (allowed: bin/todo, todo/store.py, todo/commands.py, .shapeup/todo-cli/spikes/**) — so I cannot fix the fixture text myself; flagging for GATE H / a fixture-authoring fix in the scope contract.
